$comment: Per-job wall-clock ceilings for .github/workflows/ci.yml, checked by the
'Pipeline budget' job against what the run actually took (scripts/perf/ci-budget.mjs).
Keys are job NAMES — the `name:` in the workflow, which is also what the API
reports and what .github/rulesets/main.json requires. Renaming a job without
renaming it here is reported as a stale entry, not silently ignored.
THESE FIRST NUMBERS ARE NOT MEASURED. They are each job's own declared
`timeout-minutes` multiplied by RATIO_OF_TIMEOUT (0.6): a job regularly
spending more than 60% of its kill-timeout is one bad week from being killed
by it. That makes them ceilings a run can actually breach — which is the
point, since a budget set at the timeout could never fire first — without
claiming a measurement nobody took. `--tighten` replaces them with observed
durations plus slackPercent, and can only ever lower them.
Raising a ceiling is an edit to this file with a 'why' a reviewer can
disagree with. That is deliberate: the pipeline getting slower should be a
decision somebody made, not a number that drifted.
WHEN THIS BECOMES A REQUIRED CHECK: after `npm run ci:budget -- --tighten`
has run against real runs on main and replaced the seeded numbers below with
observed ones. Until then the job goes red on the run but does not block a
merge — an unmeasured wall-clock ceiling that blocks merges is exactly the
flapping gate scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs argues against, and a gate that
flaps gets deleted. Add the context to .github/rulesets/main.json then.

run.why: wall-clock from the first job starting to the last one finishing — the number 'how long does a pull request take to go green' actually asks about. Not the sum of the jobs: they run in parallel, and a sum would grow every time a gate was moved OFF the critical path onto its own runner, which is an improvement. Seeded just above the longest single job (E2E, 18) plus room for staggered runner acquisition.

Node quality (typecheck, lint, unit, bui.why: the long pole and the one that grows: schemas:gen + tsc + eslint + two ratchets + design/i18n/docs/guidance/release gates + five fixture suites + test:unit + next build. Seeded from its 25-minute timeout. Every new `- run:` line in this job spends from here.

E2E deterministic (chromium, keyless).why: a full production build, a standalone runtime assembled the way the Dockerfile assembles it, a chromium install and four specs. Seeded from its 30-minute timeout; the Next build cache is what keeps it under, so a cache-key change shows up here first.

Python gated suite.why: pip install + the gated unittest suite. Seeded from its 10-minute timeout; pip resolution is the variable part.

Doc sync (changed source vs coupled doc).why: a full-history checkout and one dependency-free script over the diff. Seeded from its 5-minute timeout; if this ever approaches it, the checkout is the cost, not the check.

Commit convention (subjects the changelo.why: a full-history checkout and one dependency-free script over the range. Same shape and same seed as doc-sync.
